newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-More supplies seen as peso tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-More supplies seen as peso tumbles.

text.p: Philippine coconut oil sellers are expected to flood the market with more supplies this week to cash in on higher foreign exchange revenues following the drop of the peso to record levels, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"With more sellers in the market, I expect prices to drop some more after shedding an average $20 per tonne last week," said a senior Manila trader.
The peso hit a record low of 30.24 by midtrade on Monday from the previous close of 29.80.
"With the peso trading at this level, expect more aggressive exporters in the market this week," said another trader.
Traders said some 109,000 tonnes of coconut oil are booked for shipment this month, which is historically the peak month for copra harvests in the country.
"I expect coconut oil exports of around 150,000 tonnes from the Philippines and Indonesia this month, or 40,000 tonnes higher compared to world demand," said a senior trader.
"There's a lot of material for the mills so some are operating round the clock," a trader in a Philippine mill said.
Coconut oil prices are currently trading at $555 per tonne CIF, slightly higher the $539 per tonne level reached in March 1994.
